title: South Carolina Residential Builder - Online Exam Prep Course
description: South Carolina Residential Builder - Online Exam Prep Course The South Carolina Residential Builder - Online Exam Prep Course is designed for contractors preparing for the South Carolina Residential Builder technical examination. This online course supports exam preparation by helping candidates study the major residential construction topics, understand how the approved references are used, and build a more organized approach to open book testing. Residential builder exam preparation requires more than field experience. Many candidates already understand jobsite work, tools, materials, subcontractor coordination, and construction sequencing from years in the industry. The exam, however, also requires candidates to work with written references, code language, construction standards, and technical terminology. This course helps bridge the gap between hands-on experience and exam-focused study. The South Carolina Residential Builder exam is a technical examination for individuals pursuing residential builder licensure through the South Carolina Residential Builders Commission. Candidates are expected to demonstrate knowledge related to residential construction practices, code application, building materials, foundations, framing, concrete, masonry, truss handling, gypsum systems, safety, and general building procedures. An effective study plan should include both trade review and reference navigation. This online exam prep course is built to help candidates study with structure. Instead of approaching the books randomly, students can focus on the types of content that matter for contractor exam preparation. The course helps organize study time, reinforces important residential building concepts, and encourages candidates to become more comfortable using the listed reference books before exam day. The South Carolina Residential Builder exam is open book, which makes book familiarity a major part of preparation. Candidates should not wait until test day to learn where information is located. The best preparation comes from using the references during study, learning how each book is organized, reviewing important sections, and practicing how to connect exam questions to the proper source material. This course is a strong option for candidates who want flexible online study support while preparing for the South Carolina Residential Builder exam. The course can help guide review of residential code topics, carpentry and building construction principles, concrete construction, masonry, truss installation and bracing, and gypsum construction. It also helps candidates approach the exam with a more organized mindset and a better understanding of how to study from multiple technical references. Exam Details The South Carolina Residential Builder licensing examination process is administered through the South Carolina Residential Builders Commission. Individuals seeking licensure by examination must complete a two-part examination process. The first part is the Residential Builder technical examination, and the second part is the Business Management and Law for Residential Builders examination. The Residential Builder technical examination contains 110 multiple-choice questions. Applicants must obtain a passing score of 70% on the technical examination. The Business Management and Law for Residential Builders examination contains 50 multiple-choice questions, and applicants must obtain the required passing scale score for that examination. PSI Services LLC conducts the examination program for the South Carolina Residential Builders Commission. Candidates must apply to the Commission before scheduling the examination. Once the Commission approves the applicant, the candidate receives examination eligibility and may schedule the required examination through PSI. Examination eligibility is valid for one year. Candidates are allowed three attempts to pass the examination within a 12-month period. Candidates should track their eligibility window carefully and schedule their exams with enough time to complete the required testing process. The Residential Builder technical exam is based on an approved examination content outline and listed reference materials. The examination may include questions drawn from the reference books as well as questions based on trade knowledge and general industry practices. For code questions, the exam is based on the listed code edition. Candidates may use a silent, nonprinting, non-programmable calculator in the examination center. Candidates should also review PSI testing rules before the exam date so they understand identification requirements, check-in procedures, permitted materials, and testing center conduct. Open Book Test The South Carolina Residential Builder examination is an open book test. Candidates may bring approved reference books into the examination center. The references are not provided at the testing center, so candidates are responsible for bringing their own allowed materials on exam day. An open book test still requires serious preparation. Candidates must be able to move through their books efficiently, understand where major subjects are located, and recognize the terms used in exam questions. The ability to locate information quickly can be just as important as knowing the construction concept itself. This online exam prep course supports open book preparation by helping candidates study the references with purpose. Students should become familiar with the table of contents, index, chapter layout, diagrams, terminology, and common subject areas in each book. The more comfortable candidates become with their materials, the more confident they can feel when working through exam questions. Open book exams often create a false sense of security. Some candidates assume they can simply look up every answer during the test. In reality, the exam is timed, the books are technical, and many questions require judgment, understanding, and quick navigation. Strong preparation helps candidates avoid wasting time searching through unfamiliar material. For this reason, candidates should use the online course along with the reference books. The course can guide topic review, but the books remain essential tools for open book testing. A practical study plan should combine course lessons, book review, repeated navigation practice, and review of the exam content outline. Licensing Steps Applicants pursuing a South Carolina Residential Builder license by examination must begin with the South Carolina Residential Builders Commission. The Commission reviews applications and determines whether an applicant is eligible to sit for the examination. Before applying for examination approval, applicants must have one year of Commission-approved experience under the supervision of a licensee in the trade for which they are applying. This experience requirement helps confirm that applicants have practical exposure to residential building work before entering the examination process. After the application is submitted, the Commission reviews the applicant’s qualifications and documentation. Once approved, the Commission notifies the applicant and PSI. The candidate may then schedule the required examination through PSI within the eligibility period. Candidates seeking licensure by examination must pass both the Residential Builder technical examination and the Business Management and Law for Residential Builders examination. The technical exam measures residential building knowledge, while the business and law exam measures knowledge related to business practices, legal responsibilities, and management topics for residential builders. Candidates should keep all application materials, approval notices, testing information, and scheduling details organized throughout the process. Exam preparation and licensing paperwork should move together. A candidate who studies early and handles application requirements carefully can approach the licensing process with fewer avoidable delays. State Requirements The South Carolina Residential Builder license is regulated by the South Carolina Residential Builders Commission, part of the South Carolina Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation. The Commission establishes application requirements, examination requirements, experience standards, and licensing procedures for residential builders. The licensing process is intended to confirm that applicants have the minimum knowledge and experience needed to perform residential building work in a competent and responsible manner. Candidates must meet the Commission’s application requirements before testing and must complete the required examinations unless they qualify under an approved waiver pathway. South Carolina recognizes certain exam waiver options for the technical portion of the Residential Builder examination. These options may apply to qualified applicants who hold specific licenses or credentials recognized by the Commission. The Business Management and Law examination may still be required, and applicants must still meet applicable licensing requirements. Applicants should understand that passing the examination is one part of the process. Experience, application approval, documentation, testing eligibility, and Commission requirements also matter. Candidates should review state instructions carefully and make sure they are following the correct path for their license type. The online exam prep course is designed to support study for the Residential Builder technical exam. It does not replace the state application process, Commission approval, required experience, or PSI scheduling. Candidates should use the course as part of a broader plan that includes application preparation, reference review, and exam scheduling. Candidates should become familiar with its organization, chapter structure, section numbering, tables, definitions, and index. Code language can be precise, so candidates should practice reading requirements carefully and connecting questions to the correct code section. Carpentry and Building Construction supports broader residential building knowledge. Candidates can use it to review framing methods, construction materials, layout practices, structural systems, and common procedures used in residential construction. This type of general construction knowledge helps connect field experience with written exam content. The concrete, masonry, truss, and gypsum references each support specialized areas of the technical exam. Candidates should review terminology, material handling, installation requirements, quality practices, safety concerns, and common construction details within these books. These topics are important because residential builders are responsible for understanding how different building systems come together on a project. A strong study plan should include repeated review rather than one-time reading. Candidates should work through the online course, then return to the books to reinforce the material. Each study session should include active reference use. Candidates can practice finding topics, reading sections, identifying key terms, and explaining concepts in their own words. Because the exam is open book, candidates should practice using the references under timed conditions. This helps develop speed and confidence. Candidates should know which book is most likely to contain a certain topic and how to move quickly from the index or contents page to the correct section. Students should also prepare for the Business Management and Law exam separately. The online course described on this page is focused on the Residential Builder technical exam. The online format gives candidates a convenient way to prepare without relying only on independent reading. description: South Carolina Refrigeration Contractor - Online Exam Prep Course Prepare for the South Carolina Refrigeration Contractor examination with an online exam prep course focused on mechanical code requirements, refrigeration principles, air-conditioning systems, piping design, controls, maintenance, excavation awareness, and construction safety. The South Carolina Refrigeration Contractor - Online Exam Prep Course supports candidates preparing for contractor-level work involving refrigeration and related mechanical systems. The course organizes a broad range of material into manageable study areas, helping students review system operation, equipment components, piping, controls, troubleshooting, code compliance, and safe work practices. Refrigeration contractor exam preparation requires more than memorizing isolated definitions. Candidates should understand how compressors, condensers, evaporators, metering devices, refrigerants, piping, controls, airflow, and electrical components work together as a complete system. They should also be able to recognize installation requirements, diagnose common operating problems, and locate supporting information in the approved reference books. The examination is open book, making reference navigation an important part of preparation. Candidates must know which publication applies to a question, where the relevant section is located, and how to interpret tables, diagrams, formulas, code language, and technical instructions within the available testing time. This online course is intended to be used with the listed examination references. The reference books are not identified as included with the course and should be obtained separately. Candidates should study with the physical books they plan to bring to the examination so they can become familiar with each publication’s organization before test day. The listed references include the 2021 International Mechanical Code, OSHA construction regulations, the Pipefitter’s Handbook, the Carrier System Design Manual for piping design, Modern Refrigeration and Air Conditioning, the South Carolina 811 Excavator Manual, Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Technology, and the Trane Air Conditioning Manual. Together, these publications support preparation involving code compliance, heating, air conditioning, refrigeration, ventilation, equipment maintenance, system controls, pipe sizing, piping layout, excavation safety, jobsite safety, airflow, and mechanical system design. Exam Details The South Carolina Refrigeration Contractor examination contains 50 scored questions. Candidates must answer at least 35 questions correctly to pass. The examination allows three hours for completion. South Carolina Refrigeration commercial contractor candidates are also required to pass the Business Management and Law for Commercial Contractors examination. The business-law examination is separate from the Refrigeration trade examination and uses separate preparation material. The Refrigeration examination content outline includes the following subject areas: Code Compliance: 7 questions HARV General: 11 questions HARV Maintenance: 8 questions HARV Controls: 8 questions Piping - General: 3 questions Piping - Dimensioning and Design: 9 questions Safety: 4 questions HARV refers to heating, air conditioning, refrigeration, and ventilation. General preparation should include refrigeration cycles, heat transfer, refrigerants, compressors, condensers, evaporators, metering devices, airflow, equipment components, pressure-temperature relationships, and system operation. Maintenance preparation should include inspection, testing, common system symptoms, service measurements, refrigerant conditions, airflow restrictions, component performance, and troubleshooting procedures. Candidates should understand how abnormal pressures, temperatures, electrical readings, and airflow conditions can help identify a system problem. Controls preparation may include thermostats, relays, contactors, solenoids, pressure controls, temperature controls, overload devices, defrost controls, motor controls, safety switches, and sequence of operation. Students should be able to recognize the purpose of common control components and understand how they affect system performance. Piping preparation should include dimensions, fittings, pipe sizing, equivalent length, pressure drop, layout, supports, insulation, refrigerant velocity, oil return, and common design practices. Candidates should practice reading piping tables, charts, diagrams, and technical specifications accurately. Code-compliance preparation should focus on the 2021 International Mechanical Code. Relevant study may include refrigeration systems, mechanical equipment, ventilation, exhaust, ducts, piping, appliance installation, access, clearances, and other requirements associated with mechanical contractor work. Safety preparation should include OSHA construction requirements, personal protective equipment, ladders, scaffolds, fall protection, hand and power tools, electrical hazards, material handling, excavation awareness, and safe work around pressurized systems and mechanical equipment. Three hours for 50 questions provides limited time for searching through several technical publications. Candidates who are unfamiliar with the books may spend too much time in the wrong reference or overlook an applicable table, exception, or diagram. The online course supports a structured reference-navigation process. Students should first identify the subject of the question, select the most appropriate publication, locate the applicable section, review the surrounding information, and confirm the answer. The Pipefitter’s Handbook and Carrier System Design Manual support piping dimensions, fittings, sizing, layout, and design. The broader refrigeration and air-conditioning textbooks support questions involving system principles, equipment, controls, maintenance, diagnostics, airflow, electrical components, installation, and service practices. The South Carolina 811 Excavator Manual supports excavation and underground utility damage-prevention topics. Candidates should practice with all listed references nearby. Code questions may require candidates to connect a general requirement with a more specific provision. For safety, learn how to locate OSHA requirements directly in 29 CFR Part 1926. Study fall protection, ladders, tools, electrical hazards, personal protective equipment, material handling, and excavation safety. Complete timed practice sessions with the listed references nearby. How 1 Exam Prep Helps You Reach Your Goal 1 Exam Prep helps South Carolina refrigeration contractor candidates prepare through organized study guidance, trade-focused review, practice-oriented learning, reference navigation, and confidence-building structure. Exam Details The South Carolina Commercial Air Conditioning Contractor examination addresses knowledge associated with commercial air-conditioning systems and related mechanical work. Candidates should be prepared to study code requirements, refrigeration and air-conditioning principles, system sizing, duct design, fuel-gas systems, construction safety, and practical field calculations. Commercial air-conditioning work involves the interaction of many systems and components. Equipment selection must be supported by appropriate load calculations. Duct systems must be designed to deliver the required airflow. Fuel-fired equipment must comply with gas-piping, combustion-air, and venting requirements. Mechanical installations must also meet applicable code provisions and jobsite-safety expectations. Commercial load calculations consider building size, orientation, construction, occupancy, internal heat gains, ventilation, outdoor conditions, and other factors that influence heating and cooling demand. Manual D supports review of duct-system design. Air distribution depends on duct dimensions, equivalent length, fittings, pressure loss, available static pressure, airflow, and system layout. The book helps connect equipment performance with the duct system that delivers conditioned air. Manual J supports residential load-calculation review. Although the product is intended for commercial air-conditioning contractor preparation, residential load concepts remain useful for understanding the factors that influence system sizing and building heat gain or loss. A mechanical installation question may lead to the International Mechanical Code. A fuel-gas or venting question may require the International Fuel Gas Code. The course helps candidates work through the full outline instead of preparing only for familiar topics. The Swimming Pools technical examination is not the only examination involved in the commercial contractor licensing process. The qualifying party or primary qualifying party must also satisfy the applicable South Carolina business management and law examination requirement. That examination is separate from the Swimming Pools trade test and uses different study material. Open Book Test The South Carolina Swimming Pools examination is administered as an open-book test using permitted reference materials. Candidates may bring approved books that comply with PSI’s current testing rules. An open-book examination still requires substantial preparation. Candidates do not have enough time to read complete chapters while testing. They must be able to recognize the subject of a question, choose the correct reference, identify an effective index term, locate the applicable chapter or code section, review any exceptions or tables, and select the best answer within the allotted time. The online course supports this process by encouraging candidates to associate each examination category with the correct reference. Shotcrete questions should direct the candidate toward the ACI shotcrete material. Concrete questions may require Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures. Reinforcing steel questions belong in Placing Reinforcing Bars. Pool care and operation questions may require the Certified Pool-Spa Operators Handbook, while public-pool requirements should be researched in Regulation 61-51. Electrical questions focus on swimming pool wiring and related provisions found in Article 680. Excavation and underground utility topics connect with the South Carolina 811 Excavator Manual. Broader pool construction, equipment, barrier, safety, and code questions may involve the International Swimming Pool and Spa Code. Candidates should review the current PSI candidate bulletin before examination day. The bulletin establishes testing-center policies for reference books, tabs, highlighting, handwritten notes, loose papers, attachments, binding, and other book modifications. All materials brought into the examination must comply with the current rules. Licensing Steps The Swimming Pools examination is one part of the process for obtaining the applicable South Carolina contractor license. Applicants should follow the current requirements established by the South Carolina Contractor’s Licensing Board. Review the Swimming Pools classification. Confirm that the classification matches the type and scope of swimming pool work the business intends to perform. Identify the qualifying party. Determine who will serve as the qualifying party or primary qualifying party for the contractor license. Prepare for the required examinations. Study for the Swimming Pools technical examination and the applicable South Carolina business management and law examination. Schedule the examinations. Follow the current PSI registration and scheduling procedures for South Carolina contractor examinations. Complete the required tests. Meet the passing requirement for each examination associated with the requested classification. Complete the licensing application. Submit the current contractor application and qualifying-party documentation to the South Carolina Contractor’s Licensing Board. Provide supporting documentation. Submit the experience, financial, business-entity, and other materials required for the requested license classification and group. Receive licensing approval. Wait for formal approval from the Board before representing the business as licensed for regulated contractor work. Passing the Swimming Pools examination does not automatically issue a contractor license. Applicants must complete the full application process and satisfy the Board’s current licensing requirements. State Requirements The South Carolina Contractor’s Licensing Board regulates commercial general and mechanical contractors, qualifying parties, and related contractor classifications. The Swimming Pools classification applies to regulated work within the authorized scope of that classification. The qualifying party or primary qualifying party must complete the applicable examination requirements before the entity or individual submits the contractor license application. The Board currently allows candidates to schedule the required PSI examinations without obtaining examination preapproval. Applicants must also meet the Board’s current requirements involving qualification, documented experience, financial responsibility, business authorization, license group limitations, and application documentation. Requirements may differ based on the applicant’s business structure and the scope or value of work the contractor intends to perform. South Carolina also distinguishes between commercial contractor licensing and licensing or registration for professionals working solely in residential construction. Applicants should review the appropriate licensing path for the work they plan to offer. Swimming pool contractors who perform regulated commercial work generally follow the Contractor’s Licensing Board process, while certain residential-only activities may fall under the Residential Builders Commission. Public swimming pool projects are subject to South Carolina Regulation 61-51. The regulation addresses public-pool construction and operating permits, design requirements, equipment, recirculation systems, decks, water quality, sanitation, safety provisions, inspections, operation, and maintenance. Contractors preparing for public-pool work should understand that contractor licensing and facility-specific regulatory compliance are separate responsibilities. Candidates should practice using diagrams, tables, and index entries within the reinforcing bar reference. Electrical review should focus on the pool-related provisions of Article 680. Candidates should learn how Article 680 is organized and pay close attention to definitions, exceptions, and equipment-specific rules. Regulation 61-51 preparation should focus on South Carolina public swimming pool requirements. Candidates should become familiar with the regulation’s organization and practice locating provisions involving permits, design, equipment, circulation, water quality, decks, safety, inspections, operation, and maintenance. During practice, candidates should read each question carefully and identify words such as minimum, maximum, required, prohibited, permitted, except, before, and after. Frequently Asked Questions Who is the South Carolina Swimming Pool Contractor Online Exam Prep Course for? Follow the examination outline, study each category, review the corresponding reference material, complete practice-oriented review, record missed topics, and repeat timed reference searches until the books feel familiar.

Exam Details The South Carolina Wood Frame Structures Contractor examination is administered through PSI for the South Carolina Contractor’s Licensing Board. The technical examination contains 50 questions. Candidates must answer at least 35 questions correctly to meet the published passing requirement, and three hours are allowed for completion. The examination content outline is divided into six subject areas: Safety: 5 questions Concrete and Earthwork: 7 questions Concrete: 9 questions Rough Carpentry: 16 questions Manufactured Trusses: 6 questions Roofing: 7 questions Rough carpentry is the largest category, accounting for 16 of the 50 examination questions. Candidates should give substantial study time to framing terminology, structural layouts, floor systems, wall framing, roof construction, openings, sheathing, connections, fasteners, lumber characteristics, and common construction procedures. Candidates should connect these areas with the code provisions and carpentry practices involved in wood-frame construction. The manufactured-truss category includes six questions. Candidates should understand safe handling, installation, temporary restraint, permanent restraint, bracing, storage, lifting, and construction-site responsibilities involving metal plate connected wood trusses. Complete the Wood Frame Structures technical examination and the South Carolina commercial business and law examination. Submit the licensing application. State Requirements The South Carolina Contractor’s Licensing Board regulates commercial general and mechanical contractors and the individuals who serve as their qualifying parties. Wood Frame Structures is included among the general contractor building classifications. Applicants must designate a primary qualifying party for each classification or subclassification requested. The primary qualifying party is the individual principally responsible for directing or reviewing work performed under that classification. An applicant qualifying by examination must pass the appropriate technical exam before submitting the qualifying-party application. The South Carolina Business Management and Law for Commercial Contractors examination is also required before requesting qualifying-party certification. Applicants qualifying through examination must submit at least two years of relevant work experience performed within the five years preceding the application. Unless otherwise provided by the Board, the experience should primarily involve commercial work related to the requested classification. Relevant Wood Frame Structures experience may include commercial floor framing, wall framing, roof framing, structural sheathing, truss installation, concrete foundations, roofing, jobsite safety, plan interpretation, material coordination, and supervision of wood-frame construction activities. title: South Carolina Contractor License Application Service
description: South Carolina Contractor License Application Service The South Carolina Contractor License Application Service is designed for contractors, construction business owners, qualifying parties, residential builders, specialty contractors, mechanical contractors, and commercial contractors who want organized support while preparing a South Carolina contractor license application. South Carolina contractor licensing is handled through the South Carolina Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation, commonly known as SCLLR, with different boards and application paths depending on the type of work being performed. South Carolina uses a structured licensing system that separates commercial and residential contractor work. The South Carolina Contractor’s Licensing Board regulates commercial general contractors, mechanical contractors, construction managers, burglar alarm contractors, fire alarm contractors, fire sprinkler contractors, and related programs. The South Carolina Residential Builders Commission regulates residential builders, residential specialty contractors, and home inspectors. Choosing the correct board is one of the most important early steps in the application process. This service helps applicants approach the South Carolina licensing process with a clearer plan. Instead of trying to sort through commercial classifications, residential license categories, financial statements, experience requirements, PSI exam information, NASCLA questions, qualifying party details, local permit rules, and state forms alone, applicants receive structured guidance focused on preparing a cleaner and more organized application package. The goal is to help contractors understand what the board is asking for and gather the information needed before submission. The South Carolina Contractor License Application Service is helpful for first-time applicants, out-of-state contractors expanding into South Carolina, commercial contractors preparing a Contractor’s Licensing Board application, residential builders applying through the Residential Builders Commission, mechanical contractors organizing trade materials, specialty contractors reviewing license categories, and companies that need help understanding which South Carolina board applies to the work they plan to perform. South Carolina contractor licensing is not only about passing an exam. Applicants may need to select the correct board, choose the correct classification or license category, document experience, identify the applicant entity, prepare financial information, complete required examinations, organize bond or insurance documents when applicable, and satisfy final state requirements before a license or registration can be issued. Local permits and inspections may still be required after state licensing. This application service does not replace SCLLR, the Contractor’s Licensing Board, the Residential Builders Commission, PSI, any municipality, or any local building department. It does not guarantee approval, does not include government or PSI fees, and does not waive any South Carolina licensing, examination, financial, experience, insurance, bond, business registration, permit, inspection, renewal, or local requirement. 1 Exam Prep helps applicants prepare, organize, and approach the application process with a more professional workflow. What You Get Application Guidance: Support understanding the South Carolina contractor license application path based on the work your business plans to perform. Board Path Review: Help identifying whether your application may involve the South Carolina Contractor’s Licensing Board, the Residential Builders Commission, or another related licensing path. Classification and Category Planning: Guidance organizing the application around the correct commercial classification, mechanical classification, residential builder license, or residential specialty category. Experience Documentation Support: Help organizing work history, supervision, trade experience, and application details connected to the license or registration category. Financial Requirement Planning: Support organizing financial information for commercial contractor license groups when applicable. Exam Workflow Support: Guidance understanding where PSI testing, Business Management and Law exams, technical exams, NASCLA exam use, score reporting, and final application review fit into the licensing process. Submission Preparation: Support preparing a cleaner and more organized application package before the applicant submits materials to the appropriate South Carolina authority. Follow-Up Support Structure: Guidance on tracking submitted materials and organizing responses if the reviewing authority requests corrections, clarification, updated documents, or additional information. Exam Details South Carolina contractor examination requirements depend on the board, license type, and classification being pursued. Many commercial and mechanical contractor applicants work through the South Carolina Contractor’s Licensing Board and take examinations through PSI. Residential builder, residential specialty contractor, and home inspector applicants work through the Residential Builders Commission and follow that commission’s examination process. Commercial and mechanical contractor applicants commonly take a Business Management and Law examination and a technical or trade examination tied to the classification. The exact trade examination depends on the classification requested. A building contractor applicant may follow a different exam path than an electrical, plumbing, HVAC, masonry, concrete, roofing, grading, highway, or other specialty applicant. The South Carolina Contractor’s Licensing Board also recognizes the NASCLA Accredited Examination for Commercial General Building Contractors for certain commercial building paths. Applicants using the NASCLA exam should still follow South Carolina’s application, classification, financial, and final licensing requirements. Passing an accepted exam does not issue a South Carolina license by itself. Residential Builders Commission applicants seeking licensure by examination must take a two-part examination. The technical examination applies to the license or registration category, and the Business Management and Law examination covers business and legal responsibilities. Residential builder candidates take a residential builder technical examination, while residential specialty contractors take the technical examination tied to their specialty when required. South Carolina residential applicants must meet the commission’s experience requirement before applying to sit for the examination. Applicants should organize experience information carefully and make sure the experience supports the residential builder or residential specialty category being requested. The South Carolina Contractor License Application Service is not an exam-preparation course. Its purpose is application support. When an exam is required, this service helps organize that requirement within the larger licensing plan so applicants understand where testing fits into the process. Exam-prep books, courses, practice tests, and study materials are separate products when available. Open Book Test South Carolina contractor examinations administered through PSI use approved reference materials for open-book testing where listed in the current candidate bulletin. Candidates should review the PSI Candidate Information Bulletin for the exact examination they are approved to take because the approved reference list, book rules, and testing procedures vary by exam. Approved reference materials must follow PSI rules. Candidates should review the current instructions before test day so books, tabs, highlighting, indexes, and other materials comply with testing requirements. Unauthorized notes, loose papers, removable notes, unapproved books, or materials that do not meet PSI rules may be rejected at the testing center. Open-book testing does not mean the exam is easy. Applicants still need to know how to navigate the approved references quickly, apply business and law rules, understand trade topics, manage time, and answer questions tied to the license category. Strong preparation should include content-outline review, reference navigation, timed practice, and study materials matched to the approved South Carolina exam path. Licensing Steps The first step in the South Carolina contractor licensing process is identifying the type of work being performed. Commercial construction, residential construction, mechanical work, specialty contracting, alarm work, fire sprinkler work, construction management, home inspection, and residential specialty work may each follow different requirements. The correct path depends on the work category and the board that regulates it. The next step is determining whether the applicant should apply through the Contractor’s Licensing Board or the Residential Builders Commission. The Contractor’s Licensing Board handles commercial general and mechanical contractor licensing, construction manager registration, burglar and fire alarm contractor licensing, fire sprinkler licensing, and related programs. The Residential Builders Commission handles residential builders, residential specialty contractors, and home inspectors. After the board path is identified, the applicant should select the correct classification or license category. Commercial applicants should review the general contractor, mechanical contractor, and specialty classifications that match the work they plan to perform. Residential applicants should review whether they need a residential builder license or a residential specialty contractor registration or license category. Commercial applicants should also review the license group or financial level connected to the work they plan to perform. South Carolina commercial contractor licensing uses financial qualification levels tied to the size of projects the contractor may undertake. Applicants should prepare financial documents that support the license group requested. The applicant should then organize experience information. Residential applicants must document qualifying experience before examination eligibility. Commercial and mechanical applicants may also need to organize experience, qualifying-party information, or classification-specific background details depending on the license path. Experience should match the classification or license category being requested. Business information should be organized before submission. Common application items may include legal business name, trade name when applicable, business entity type, owner or officer information, responsible party information, mailing address, physical address, phone number, email address, federal employer identification number when applicable, and business registration records. The business name should be consistent across application forms, financial documents, insurance records, bond documents, contracts, and permits. If examinations are required, the applicant should review the exam workflow carefully. Some applicants must receive approval before testing, while others must follow specific scheduling procedures through PSI. Applicants should register only for the examination connected to the approved classification or license category. Applicants should also review insurance, bond, and financial responsibility requirements. Depending on the license type, project type, local authority, or business structure, applicants may need insurance certificates, surety bond documents, financial statements, or other supporting materials. Documents should match the legal business name used on the application. After the application package is complete, the applicant submits materials to the appropriate South Carolina board or commission. Missing financial documents, inconsistent business names, unsupported experience, wrong classification selection, absent exam records, incomplete forms, missing signatures, or incorrect board selection can delay review. After submission, the applicant should monitor application status and respond promptly if the board requests corrections, clarification, updated documents, or additional information. Contractors should keep copies of submitted materials, exam records, financial documents, license records, insurance certificates, permits, inspection documents, and agency communications for their records. State Requirements South Carolina contractor requirements are handled through a combination of board licensing, commission licensing, classification rules, financial qualifications, examination requirements, business records, insurance or bond documents when applicable, and local permit rules. Contractors should not treat these requirements as interchangeable. Commercial Contractor Licensing is handled by the South Carolina Contractor’s Licensing Board. Commercial general contractors and mechanical contractors should review the board’s classification, financial, examination, and application requirements before bidding, contracting for, or performing covered work. Residential Builder Licensing is handled by the South Carolina Residential Builders Commission. Residential builder applicants should follow the commission’s experience, examination, application, and final licensing requirements. Residential Specialty Contractor Requirements may apply to specific residential trades or specialties. Applicants should review the commission’s category requirements before offering or performing specialty residential work. Business Management and Law Examination Requirements apply to many South Carolina contractor license paths. Applicants should use the exam instructions tied to the board, commission, and license category involved. Technical Examination Requirements may apply depending on the classification or license category. The technical exam should match the work the applicant intends to perform. NASCLA Exam Recognition may apply for certain commercial building applicants. Applicants using the NASCLA examination must still satisfy South Carolina application, financial, classification, and final licensing requirements. Financial Qualification Requirements apply to commercial contractor license groups. Applicants should prepare financial documents carefully and make sure the documents support the group requested. Business Entity Requirements may also apply. A corporation, limited liability company, partnership, sole proprietorship using a trade name, or out-of-state business may need proper registration before or alongside the contractor license application. Business records should match license applications, financial documents, insurance certificates, tax records, contracts, and permit documents. Local Permits and Inspections remain separate from state licensing. Even after a South Carolina contractor license is issued, specific projects may still require building permits, trade permits, plan review, zoning approval, inspections, or other local approvals before work begins. State fees, local application fees, license fees, exam fees, renewal fees, financial document costs, insurance costs, bond costs, business registration fees, permit fees, inspection fees, and other government or third-party charges are separate from this application service unless a product listing clearly states otherwise. Applicants should be prepared to pay required fees directly to the proper agency, board, commission, municipality, testing provider, insurer, financial professional, bonding company, or other authority. Test Information and Study Materials South Carolina contractor applicants should use study materials that match the exact board, classification, license category, and exam path involved. A commercial building applicant may need different preparation than a residential builder, mechanical contractor, electrical contractor, plumbing contractor, HVAC contractor, fire sprinkler contractor, alarm contractor, or residential specialty contractor. The Business Management and Law examination focuses on contractor business responsibilities, licensing rules, contracts, project management, financial responsibilities, labor responsibilities, safety, tax topics, and South Carolina-specific construction business practices. Applicants should review the current candidate bulletin and use materials tied to the correct exam. Technical examinations focus on the trade or classification being requested. These exams may address codes, standards, installation practices, estimating, plan reading, materials, equipment, safety, and trade-specific procedures. The correct study materials depend on the examination connected to the applicant’s license path. Residential builder applicants should prepare for both the technical examination and the Business Management and Law examination. Residential specialty applicants should prepare for the technical examination tied to the specialty and the business law portion when required. Commercial applicants should review whether the South Carolina exam or NASCLA exam path applies to the classification requested. Because South Carolina exams use approved references where listed, applicants should prepare by learning how to locate information efficiently. Good preparation includes reviewing the content outline, organizing approved books under PSI rules, practicing timed questions, and building confidence with the reference materials before test day. This application service helps applicants organize the licensing paperwork that surrounds the exam process. For applicants who also need exam preparation, separate study products may be useful. Those products should match the South Carolina board, classification, exam name, and approved reference list connected to the applicant’s license path. How 1 Exam Prep Helps You Reach Your Goal 1 Exam Prep helps South Carolina contractor applicants approach the licensing process with structure and confidence. The South Carolina contractor application process can feel detailed because it may involve board selection, classification review, residential or commercial path planning, experience documentation, financial qualification, PSI examination workflow, NASCLA questions, insurance or bond planning, local permit requirements, and final state review. This service helps organize those pieces so applicants can move forward with a clearer plan. This can be especially useful for contractors who are experienced in construction but unfamiliar with South Carolina’s licensing paperwork. 1 Exam Prep supports applicants through practical application guidance rather than unrealistic promises. This service does not guarantee license approval, exam results, faster processing, board acceptance, permit approval, or any state or local decision. South Carolina licensing boards, testing providers, municipalities, and local building departments control their own requirements and final approvals. 1 Exam Prep’s role is to support applicants with organized preparation, licensing guidance, document planning, and confidence-building structure throughout the application process. What is the South Carolina Contractor License Application Service? The South Carolina Contractor License Application Service is a professional application support service that helps contractors prepare and organize a South Carolina contractor license, residential builder license, specialty license, or related application package. It focuses on board path review, classification planning, document organization, exam workflow support, and submission preparation. Who issues South Carolina contractor licenses? South Carolina contractor licensing is handled through SCLLR. Commercial contractor licensing is handled by the Contractor’s Licensing Board, and residential builder and residential specialty licensing is handled by the Residential Builders Commission. What is the difference between the Contractor’s Licensing Board and the Residential Builders Commission? The Contractor’s Licensing Board handles commercial general contractors, mechanical contractors, construction managers, alarm contractors, fire sprinkler contractors, and related programs. The Residential Builders Commission handles residential builders, residential specialty contractors, and home inspectors. Do South Carolina contractor applicants need to take an exam? Many South Carolina contractor applicants must pass a Business Management and Law examination and a technical or trade examination. The exact exams depend on the board, license type, classification, and category requested. Are South Carolina contractor exams open book? South Carolina contractor exams administered through PSI use approved references for open-book testing where listed in the current candidate bulletin. Applicants should follow the PSI bulletin for the exact exam, reference list, and testing rules. Does South Carolina accept the NASCLA exam? South Carolina recognizes the NASCLA Accredited Examination for Commercial General Building Contractors for certain commercial building paths. Applicants must still satisfy South Carolina application, classification, financial, and final licensing requirements. Does this service include exam preparation? No. This product is an application service. It helps with application organization, document planning, and licensing workflow guidance. Exam-prep courses, books, practice tests, and study materials are separate products when available. Does this service include the fee paid to the state? No. State fees are not included in the South Carolina Contractor License Application Service. Application fees, PSI examination fees, license fees, renewal fees, financial document costs, permit fees, insurance costs, bond costs, and other government or third-party charges are separate. Can this service help with South Carolina classification selection? Yes. This service can help applicants organize the application around the classification, license category, or board path that matches the work they intend to perform. The board or commission makes the final decision on license approval. Can out-of-state contractors apply for a South Carolina contractor license? Yes. Out-of-state contractors may apply for South Carolina contractor licensure when they plan to perform work that requires a South Carolina license. Business registration, application documentation, exams, financial information, and final licensing requirements must be handled according to South Carolina rules. Can 1 Exam Prep guarantee that my South Carolina contractor license will be approved? No. License approval is controlled by the South Carolina licensing board or commission reviewing the application. This service helps applicants prepare and organize the application package, but it does not guarantee approval, processing time, exam results, permit approval, or any state or local decision. Why should I use an application service instead of applying alone? An application service helps reduce confusion, organize paperwork, and create a clearer path through South Carolina’s contractor licensing process. Many contractors know their trade well but prefer support when dealing with board selection, classification questions, financial documents, experience records, PSI testing workflow, NASCLA questions, business records, and submission details.

title: South Carolina Public Swimming Pools, Regulation 61-51
description: SOUTH CAROLINA PUBLIC SWIMMING POOLS, REGULATION 61-51The *South Carolina Public Swimming Pools, Regulation 61-51*, available from 1 Exam Prep, is the official state regulation issued by the South Carolina Department of Health and Environmental Control (DHEC) governing the design, construction, operation, and maintenance of public swimming pools and spas. This regulation establishes minimum safety and sanitation standards, including requirements for water quality, filtration systems, chemical handling, fencing, circulation equipment, and inspection procedures. It is a mandatory reference for the South Carolina Swimming Pool Contractor licensing examination administered by PSI. Regulation 61-51 aligns with national standards from the *Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)* and the *Model Aquatic Health Code (MAHC)*, ensuring compliance with South Carolina’s public health and safety codes for pool contractors and facility operators. South Carolina Regulation 61-51 was enacted to protect public health and safety in public swimming pools. The regulation is a helpful resource for swimming pool contractors and certified pool operators. 45 pages. (2023)

title: South Carolina Swimming Pool Contractor Exam Complete Book Package
description: South Carolina Swimming Pool Contractor Exam Complete Book Package Prepare for the South Carolina Swimming Pool Contractor examination with a complete collection of trade references selected for the PSI-administered licensing test. This package brings together the technical manuals, construction references, state regulations, electrical provisions, pool-operation guidance, excavation information, and swimming pool code material associated with the examination. The South Carolina Swimming Pool Contractor Exam Complete Book Package is designed for contractors, qualifying parties, construction professionals, pool builders, and experienced tradespeople preparing to demonstrate their knowledge of swimming pool construction and operation. Instead of searching for each reference separately, candidates receive the core books in one organized package. The examination covers several distinct areas of knowledge. Candidates may need to locate information involving shotcrete application, concrete materials, reinforcing steel, pool electrical systems, public swimming pool regulations, pool care and operation, excavation practices, code requirements, and estimating. Having the correct references available allows candidates to build a structured study plan around the subjects identified in the examination outline. This package is especially useful for candidates who want to practice finding information directly within the source material. Contractor examinations often require more than memorizing definitions. Candidates must understand how each reference is organized, recognize which book addresses a particular subject, interpret technical language, and move efficiently between chapters, tables, diagrams, regulations, and index entries. Each included book serves a specific purpose. The concrete and shotcrete references address materials and placement practices. The reinforcing steel reference supports questions involving bar placement and structural reinforcement. Regulation 61-51 addresses South Carolina requirements for public swimming pools. The pool operator handbook covers practical concepts related to water quality, circulation, sanitation, maintenance, and facility operation. Article 680 addresses electrical requirements associated with swimming pools and similar installations. The South Carolina 811 manual covers safe excavation and underground utility notification practices. The International Swimming Pool and Spa Code provides code-based requirements for pool and spa construction, safety, equipment, and related systems. Studying with the complete set helps candidates connect related concepts. A question about a pool shell may involve concrete properties, reinforcement, and shotcrete placement. A question about equipment installation may require knowledge of pool operation, electrical safety, and code requirements. A question involving site preparation may connect excavation responsibilities with construction planning. Preparing with the complete reference library supports a broader understanding of how these subjects work together on an actual swimming pool project. What You Get Guide to Shotcrete / Shotcrete Guide ACI 506 Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures, 17th Edition Placing Reinforcing Bars, Recommended Practices, 10th Edition Public Swimming Pools, Regulation 61-51 Certified Pool-Spa Operators Handbook Article 680, National Electrical Code: Swimming Pool Wiring, 2020 South Carolina 811 Excavator Manual International Swimming Pool and Spa Code, 2021 This is a book package for the South Carolina Swimming Pool Contractor trade examination. It does not include the separate South Carolina Business Management and Law reference unless that material is specifically added to the order. Exam Details The South Carolina Swimming Pool Contractor technical examination is administered through PSI for the South Carolina Contractor’s Licensing Board. The examination contains 50 questions. Candidates must answer at least 35 questions correctly to earn a passing score, and the allotted testing time is three hours. The official examination content outline distributes questions across seven subject areas: Pool Electrical: 6 questions Shotcrete: 8 questions Concrete: 6 questions Concrete Reinforcing Steel: 6 questions Pool Care and Operation: 12 questions Regulation 61-51: Swimming Pools: 8 questions Pool Estimating: 4 questions Commercial contractor candidates seeking the Swimming Pools classification are required to pass the applicable South Carolina Business Management and Law for Contractors examination in addition to the Swimming Pool technical examination. The business and law examination is separate from the trade examination and uses its own reference material. The content outline shows why a complete reference package matters. Pool care and operation represents the largest portion of the technical examination, while shotcrete, concrete, reinforcing steel, public pool regulations, electrical work, and estimating make up the remaining questions. Candidates should prepare across the entire outline rather than concentrating on a single construction subject. Open Book Test The South Carolina Swimming Pool Contractor examination follows an open-book format using approved references. Open book does not mean that candidates will have enough time to read entire chapters during the test. Successful preparation depends on becoming familiar with the layout and terminology of each book before examination day. Candidates should know which reference is most likely to contain the answer to a particular type of question. Shotcrete questions should direct attention toward the ACI shotcrete guide. Concrete mixture questions belong in the concrete reference. Reinforcing bar questions should lead to the reinforcing steel manual. Operational questions may require the pool operator handbook, while South Carolina public-pool requirements should be located in Regulation 61-51. Electrical questions on the trade examination focus on Article 680 of the 2020 National Electrical Code material. Effective open-book preparation includes reviewing each table of contents, index, glossary, chapter structure, appendix, and major technical table. Candidates should practice identifying key terms from a question and translating them into likely index entries. For example, a question may use a jobsite term while the book indexes the subject under a technical term. Familiarity with both terms can reduce search time. Books brought into the examination must comply with current PSI testing rules. Candidates should review the latest candidate bulletin before the test for policies governing permitted references, tabs, highlighting, handwritten notes, loose papers, and other materials. Licensing Steps The examination is one part of the South Carolina commercial contractor licensing process. Candidates should begin by reviewing the current requirements published by the South Carolina Contractor’s Licensing Board for the Swimming Pools classification. Review the classification requirements. Confirm that the Swimming Pools classification matches the scope of work the business intends to perform. Prepare for the required examinations. Commercial Swimming Pool Contractor candidates must complete the required business and law examination and the Swimming Pool technical examination. Register for testing. Follow the current PSI registration procedures for the South Carolina contractor examination program. Complete the examinations. Meet the passing requirements for each examination applicable to the classification. Submit the license application. Apply to the South Carolina Contractor’s Licensing Board using the current application and supporting documents. Provide required qualification documentation. Commercial contractor applicants must satisfy the Board’s current experience, financial, and qualifying-party requirements for the license group requested. Maintain the license. After approval, follow all current renewal, classification, and compliance requirements established by the Board. Passing an examination does not by itself issue a contractor license. Applicants must complete the licensing process and receive approval from the South Carolina Contractor’s Licensing Board before representing themselves as licensed for regulated commercial swimming pool work. State Requirements The South Carolina Contractor’s Licensing Board regulates general and mechanical contractors and the related commercial classifications under its authority. The Swimming Pools classification applies to regulated pool and spa construction work within the classification’s authorized scope. South Carolina distinguishes between commercial contractor licensing and licensing for businesses engaged solely in residential construction. A license issued by the Contractor’s Licensing Board may authorize commercial work and applicable residential work within the approved classification and license group. A business working only in residential construction may fall under the South Carolina Residential Builders Commission. Applicants should select the licensing path that corresponds to the work they intend to perform. Commercial license applicants must satisfy the Board’s current qualification requirements. These may involve examination results, documented experience, a designated qualifying party, financial documentation, the requested license group, application forms, and other materials required by the Board. Public swimming pool construction and alterations are also subject to South Carolina Regulation 61-51. The regulation addresses construction and operating permits, design requirements, equipment, water quality, recirculation systems, decks, safety provisions, inspections, operation, and maintenance for public swimming pool facilities. Contractors working on public pools must account for both contractor-licensing obligations and the requirements that apply to the facility itself. Reference Books Guide to Shotcrete / Shotcrete Guide ACI 506This reference addresses the materials, equipment, properties, procedures, application methods, testing concepts, and quality considerations associated with shotcrete. It supports preparation for questions involving wet-mix and dry-mix processes, placement practices, surface preparation, curing, reinforcement, and construction quality. Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures, 17th EditionThis concrete technology reference explains concrete materials, mixture proportioning, batching, mixing, placing, curing, durability, strength, and performance. It helps candidates review how cementitious materials, aggregates, water, admixtures, environmental conditions, and construction practices affect finished concrete. Placing Reinforcing Bars, Recommended Practices, 10th EditionThis manual presents established practices for placing reinforcing bars, bar supports, welded wire reinforcement, splices, clearances, bends, placement tolerances, and related field procedures. It supports the reinforcing steel portion of the swimming pool examination. Public Swimming Pools, Regulation 61-51This South Carolina regulation addresses the construction, permitting, design, equipment, operation, maintenance, and safety of public swimming pools. Candidates can use it to study state-specific requirements involving pool types, recirculation, decks, water quality, operating permits, equipment changes, inspections, and facility operation. Certified Pool-Spa Operators HandbookThis handbook covers practical pool and spa operation, including circulation, filtration, disinfection, water balance, testing, contamination response, maintenance, safety, calculations, and facility management. It is especially important for the pool care and operation portion of the examination. Article 680, National Electrical Code: Swimming Pool Wiring, 2020This reference focuses on the electrical provisions associated with swimming pools, spas, hot tubs, fountains, and similar installations. Topics include grounding, bonding, wiring methods, equipment locations, receptacles, luminaires, disconnecting means, and electrical safety around water. South Carolina 811 Excavator ManualThis manual explains South Carolina excavation notification practices and the responsibilities associated with protecting underground facilities. It supports preparation involving locate requests, utility markings, safe digging practices, communication, damage prevention, and excavation response procedures. International Swimming Pool and Spa Code, 2021This model code contains provisions for the design, construction, alteration, repair, maintenance, and safety of swimming pools, spas, hot tubs, aquatic recreation facilities, and related equipment. It addresses barriers, circulation systems, decks, structural requirements, suction fittings, accessibility-related provisions, and other pool and spa code topics. Test Information and Study Materials A strong study plan should follow the examination outline and assign preparation time according to the number of questions in each subject. Pool care and operation deserves significant attention because it represents 12 of the 50 questions. Shotcrete and Regulation 61-51 each account for eight questions. Electrical, concrete, and reinforcing steel contain six questions each, while estimating contains four. Begin by reviewing the table of contents and index in every reference. Create a mental map of the package: which book covers water chemistry, which addresses concrete performance, where electrical bonding is discussed, where South Carolina public-pool rules appear, and where reinforcement placement practices can be found. Next, study one examination category at a time. Read the major sections, identify technical terms, and practice locating answers. Use practice questions to develop a repeatable search method: identify the subject, select the correct book, choose an index term, locate the relevant section, and confirm the answer in context. Do not rely only on tabs. Tabs can help identify major chapters, but the index is often more useful for detailed questions. A candidate should also understand the difference between similar topics. Concrete mixture design belongs in a different source than reinforcing bar placement. Pool operating procedures belong in a different source than state construction requirements. Choosing the correct book quickly is one of the most important open-book testing skills. During the examination, read every question carefully and pay attention to words such as minimum, maximum, required, permitted, prohibited, except, and most appropriate. These words can change the meaning of the question. When using a code or regulation, review nearby exceptions, notes, tables, and definitions before selecting an answer. How 1 Exam Prep Helps You Reach Your Goal 1 Exam Prep supports contractor candidates with an organized, trade-focused approach to examination preparation. The South Carolina Swimming Pool Contractor Exam Complete Book Package brings the required subject areas together so candidates can spend less time searching for individual references and more time learning how to use them. Preparation should build both knowledge and reference-navigation skills. 1 Exam Prep encourages candidates to study the examination outline, work through each technical category, practice finding information under time limits, and become comfortable moving between multiple references. The package supports review of pool construction, concrete, shotcrete, reinforcing steel, electrical requirements, operation and maintenance, public-pool regulations, excavation practices, code compliance, and estimating. This structure helps candidates identify weaker subjects and create a more balanced study schedule. Open-book examinations reward preparation. Knowing where an answer is located can be as important as remembering the underlying concept. By studying with the books associated with the examination, candidates can build familiarity with chapter layouts, indexes, terminology, tables, and code sections before test day. 1 Exam Prep also helps candidates approach preparation with a clear routine: understand the exam outline, organize the references, study by topic, practice navigation, review missed questions, and repeat the process until locating information feels natural. This method promotes confidence without promising a particular examination or licensing outcome. Frequently Asked Questions What books are included in the South Carolina Swimming Pool Contractor package? The package includes the Guide to Shotcrete, Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures, Placing Reinforcing Bars, Regulation 61-51, the Certified Pool-Spa Operators Handbook, Article 680 from the 2020 National Electrical Code material, the South Carolina 811 Excavator Manual, and the 2021 International Swimming Pool and Spa Code. Is the South Carolina Swimming Pool Contractor exam open book? Yes. The technical examination uses an open-book format with approved reference materials. Candidates remain responsible for following PSI rules regarding which books and modifications are permitted in the testing room. How many questions are on the Swimming Pool Contractor exam? The examination contains 50 questions. Candidates must answer at least 35 questions correctly to pass. How much time is allowed for the exam? Candidates are allowed three hours to complete the South Carolina Swimming Pool Contractor technical examination. Does this package include the Business Management and Law book? No. This package contains the references for the Swimming Pool Contractor technical examination. The South Carolina Business Management and Law examination is separate and uses its own reference material. Which electrical material is tested? The Swimming Pool examination reference list identifies the 2020 National Electrical Code with South Carolina modifications or the corresponding handbook material, with the examination covering Article 680. This package includes the Article 680 swimming pool wiring material listed in the package contents. Why is Regulation 61-51 included? Regulation 61-51 contains South Carolina requirements for public swimming pools. Eight questions in the examination outline are assigned to this regulation, making it an important state-specific reference. Can I become licensed by passing only the trade exam? No. Commercial Swimming Pool Contractor candidates must complete the required examinations and satisfy the South Carolina Contractor’s Licensing Board application requirements. Passing the test is one part of the licensing process. How should I study for an open-book contractor exam? Study by examination category, learn which reference covers each topic, review the index and table of contents of every book, and practice locating answers under timed conditions. Familiarity with the books is essential because there is not enough time to read large sections during the examination. Who is this package designed for? This package is designed for commercial contractor candidates, qualifying parties, pool construction professionals, and tradespeople preparing for the South Carolina Swimming Pool Contractor technical examination.

Identify the major chapters, common terms, and type of information found in each reference.
